body:
AUDIT OF EVERY COMPILE-TIME TRIPWIRE IN THE REPO, and the result CLOSES a worry I raised rather than
confirming it. I said the vacuous-typeChecks pattern I hit "generalises to every compile-time
tripwire in the repo, and I would guess we have others". I went and checked. MY GUESS WAS WRONG.

WHAT I SCREENED: all 38 typeChecks snippets outside worktree copies, extracted by parsing the string
literal argument rather than eyeballing. 18 are complex enough - multi-line, or two or more calls -
to fail for a reason unrelated to the member under test, which is the mechanism that made mine
vacuous.

BUT COMPLEXITY IS THE RISK FACTOR, NOT THE DEFECT. Every complex site I checked is MITIGATED by a
same-shape positive control:
  ResolutionSuite  probes .value/.get/._1/productElement/unapply on Conditional, then asserts
                   `Conditional(0.5, res(1.0, 0.0)).whenResolved` DOES typecheck - "Control: the
                   accessors that should exist do."
  SignatureSuite   ten negative probes, two positive controls of the same shape on the same values.
  The three Unforgeable suites (amr-interop, proposition, story) are ALL positive assertions plus
  their negatives, in the same multi-line import-bearing style.

AND I TESTED THE ONE SITE WITH NO CONTROL AT ALL rather than assuming it was broken:
BirthdayInterviewSuite:251, `!typeChecks("scores.internalRatio.value")`. I inserted two temporary
positive controls in the same context:
  typeChecks("scores.internalRatio.whenResolved") = TRUE
  typeChecks("scores.internalRatio.resolution")   = TRUE
So the probe context genuinely sees `scores`, and the negative probe really is testing the absence
of `.value`. NOT VACUOUS. Probe removed; the file is untouched.

SO THE FINDING IS ABOUT ME, NOT THE REPO. The practice of pairing a negative probe with a same-shape
positive control ALREADY EXISTS here and is followed almost everywhere. I wrote a complex multi-line
snippet with no control, which is the one combination the codebase had otherwise avoided. The repo
taught the rule; I did not read it before writing.

WORTH WRITING DOWN ANYWAY, because the reason it works is not obvious from the examples: a positive
control is not decoration on a negative probe, it is the ONLY thing that distinguishes "this member
is absent" from "this snippet does not compile". `typeChecks` returns false for both. The control
must share the SHAPE of the negative probe - same value, same context, same construction - or it
tests a different question. ResolutionSuite's control is exactly that and is why its five probes are
sound despite being complex.

Suggest one line in AGENTS.md near the unforgeable-type material: every `!typeChecks` assertion
ships with a `typeChecks` assertion on a member that DOES exist, on the same value in the same
context. One line, and it is already the house style - it just is not written down.

Nothing changed in the repo from this audit; it is a read-only result. My three candidates are
unchanged and still queued: e6d0cc5, 067e35b, 57af23b.
